newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel rally continues on prompt demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel rally continues on prompt demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil continued its rally on Wednesday on sustained buying interest for prompt product and tight regional supplies, traders said.

A trader bid for a 150,000-barrels mid-December lifting cargo at $31.60 per barrel, fob, up 10 cents from Tuesday's new traded five-year high. A major offered 220,000 barrels also for mid-December loading at $31.80 fob.

China has also stepped up its purchases on the heels of the spiralling prices. Earlier this week it bought a 30,000-tonne December cargo at $241 a tonne on a c-and-f basis, up about $5 from the previous deal done last week.
The swaps market reflected the strong buying interest for prompt gas oil barrels with December swaps traded to a high of $31.40 a barrel late in the day, up almost 50 cents from Tuesday.
The sharp increases raised the prospect of western arbitrage exports to Asia as the East-West spread has widen to about $14.50 a tonne in favour of the East.

Jet fuel fell as sellers returned to the market on talks that North Asia requirements were covered. The jet fuel/gas oil swaps spread was quoted lower due to the strong gas oil prices with several offers seen for December at $1.90, down 40 cents.

The light distillates were quiet with most Singapore cargoes for lifting in December already committed. A European major confirmed being awarded the January Taiwan buy tender for unleaded 95-octane reformate at $26.80 a barrel c-and-f Taiwan.

The first cargo from the new Chinese Dalian refinery was said sold at $$1.50 a barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, fob lifting mid-December of 30,000 tonnes of 90-octane gasoline. Traders said the cargo was heading to Singapore.
Naphtha edged up further in a tight prompt market with December swaps firmer at $23.55/$23.80, from $23.30/$23.50 on Tuesday. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
